plugins.description: Persistent long-term memory for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh), powered by HydraDB.
plugins.readme_text: # HydraDB DeepSeek Harness Plugin Persistent, cross-session memory for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`), powered by [HydraDB](https://hydradb.com). It recalls relevant context before each turn, syncs your workspace docs into HydraDB, and captures conversations as durable memory, over the same shared engine (`scripts/plugin.mjs`) as the HydraDB Claude Code / Codex / OpenClaw plugins. ## What's dsh-specific here - **Entry module:** `index.js`, an ordinary [Cordis](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin (`export const name` + `export function apply(ctx)`). dsh mounts it by package name and calls `apply` with the plugin `ctx`; it registers listeners on the harness interception seams over the shared engine. - **Env prefix:** per the shared client contract, this client reads the canonical `HYDRADB_*` names plus the `HYDRA_DEEPSEEK_*` prefix (see `CONTRACT.md`). - **Skills:** the shared HydraDB skills under `skills/` for manual recall/ingest. ## Seams | dsh extension point | Engine action | |---|---| | `agent/created` | sync workspace docs into HydraDB when a session opens | | `agent/pre-step` (turn's first step) | recall relevant memory/knowledge and **prepend it to the step messages** | | `tools/post-execute` (file-writing tools) | incremental workspace sync | | `session/event` → `turn/end` | capture the completed turn | Prompt-time auto-recall (`agent/pre-step`) and workspace sync work out of the box. The `agent/pre-step` waterfall is cooperative: the plugin awaits `next()` and only prepends a user-role context message to the downstream `enter` decision, so it composes with other pre-step listeners instead of overriding them. ## Prerequisites - Node.js >= 18 - A HydraDB account: API key + database ([hydradb.com](https://hydradb.com)) - DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) ## Install This package ships as a dsh **bundle** (`dsh.bundle` + `cordis.patch.yml`), so `dsh plugin add` installs and wires it as a profile layer in one step: ```sh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-hydradb ``` dsh appends it to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` and inserts the `hydradb` plugin row automatically - no manual `cordis.patch.yml` editing. To pass config inline instead of via the environment, add a `config:` block to the bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` (see `dsh.config.example.yml` for the `--patch` overlay form). Credentials come from the plugin config (`api_key`, `database`, optional `collection`/`base_url`) or the environment: ```bash export HYDRADB_API_KEY="your-api-key" export HYDRADB_DATABASE="your-database" # dsh-prefixed names also work: HYDRA_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY / HYDRA_DEEPSEEK_TENANT_ID ``` The default search mode is `memory`; set `HYDRADB_SEARCH_MODE=both` if you also want synced workspace knowledge to auto-recall. ## Usage - **Automatic recall** runs before each turn's first step via `agent/pre-step` and prepends relevant memory/knowledge to the step messages. - The shared skills provide manual `query` / `ingest` / `doctor` / `setup` / `last-recall` actions; the contract's canonical slash form is `/hydradb-query`, `/hydradb-ingest`, `/hydradb-list`, `/hydradb-inspect`, `/hydradb-delete`. ## Configuration Config keys, environment overrides, and capture/search/ingest modes are identical to the other HydraDB plugins - see `config.example.json` and `CONTRACT.md`. ## Verified Tested against DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) 0.2.0-rc.2: the bundle installs via `dsh plugin add`, registers as a profile layer, and its `apply` seams activate cleanly. A live `dsh headless` turn (OpenRouter provider) answered a question from HydraDB memory recalled and injected through `agent/pre-step`. ## License [Apache 2.0](LICENSE) - Copyright (c) 2026 HydraDB

plugins.description: ChatGPT subscription / GPT provider for DeepSeek Harness desktop: image input, host tools and DeepSeek/GPT switching. Harness 桌面版 ChatGPT 订阅适配器，支持图片、工具调用和模型切换。Community MIT plugin.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH ChatGPT Adapter

**把 ChatGPT 订阅带进 DeepSeek Harness。登录账户，选择 GPT，即可开始工作。** 无需 API Key，支持 GPT / DeepSeek 切换、图片理解，以及 Harness 的文件、搜索和终端工具。 **仅适用于 DeepSeek Harness。** 本插件不能安装到 DeepSeek 普通网页版、手机 App 或普通聊天桌面客户端中。支持 Harness 桌面版 ≥0.2.0-rc.2 / macOS；当前实测基线为 0.2.0-rc.2。 [快速开始](#快速开始) · [使用文档](docs/INSTALLATION.md) · [下载安装包](https://github.com/diwer/dsh-codex-adapter/releases/latest) · [English](README.en.md) ## 为什么使用 - **用自己的订阅**：通过 OpenAI 页面登录授权，无需配置 API Key。 - **两种模型，随时选择**：在会话中切换 GPT 与 DeepSeek，也可让新会话默认使用 GPT。 - **图片与工具一起用**：向支持图片的模型提问，使用 Harness 内置工具读取文件、编辑代码、搜索和运行命令。 - **思考强度可调**：在模型菜单中选择推理等级，档位与默认值自动匹配当前模型。 - **连接后即可选模型**：自动加载当前账户的可用模型，支持添加和切换多个账户。 - **插件独立代理**：在订阅设置页选择直连、环境变量或自定义 HTTP(S) 代理，支持测试连接，保存后立即生效。 - **免费开源**：MIT 许可；插件不额外收费。模型权限与使用额度取决于你的 ChatGPT 账户。 ## 快速开始 适用于 **DeepSeek Harness 桌面版 ≥0.2.0-rc.2 / macOS**，需要可使用订阅模型的 ChatGPT 账户。 ### 1. 安装插件 在 **Plugins → Add plugin** 中填入： ```text dsh-codex-official-adapter@0.1.8 ``` Registry 选择 **npm 官方源（https://registry.npmjs.org/）**，点击 **Install**。完成后，等当前任务结束，完全退出并重新打开 Harness。 > 若找不到切换源的入口，或安装失败，使用[终端安装或本地包安装](docs/INSTALLATION.md#其他安装方式)。 ### 2. 连接 ChatGPT 打开 **Settings → ChatGPT 订阅 → 连接 ChatGPT**，点击 **打开授权页面**，在 OpenAI 页面完成登录与授权。返回 Harness 后会自动显示连接状态和可用模型。 ### 3. 开始使用 新建会话，在模型选择器的 **ChatGPT plan (Sign in with ChatGPT)** 下选择模型。 试着输入：`帮我阅读当前项目，说明它的用途。` 支持图片的模型也可以直接接收会话中添加的图片。 ## 常见问题 **这个插件支持哪个产品？** 仅支持 DeepSeek Harness。DeepSeek 普通网页版、手机 App 和普通聊天桌面客户端不支持安装本插件。支持 Harness 桌面版 ≥0.2.0-rc.2 / macOS；当前实测基线为 0.2.0-rc.2。 **如何在 DeepSeek Harness 中使用 ChatGPT 订阅？** 安装 `dsh-codex-official-adapter@0.1.8`，在设置中连接自己的 ChatGPT 账户，再从 ChatGPT plan 中选择模型。无需 API Key，模型权限与额度由账户决定。 **可以直接填 GitHub 地址吗？** 这是源码地址：`https://github.com/diwer/dsh-codex-adapter`。不同宿主与市场的安装器支持有差异，日常安装建议使用上面的明确包名与版本。 **已经连接，却没有模型？** 点击“刷新模型”，检查当前账户的订阅权限、额度及网络。模型列表以账户实际返回为准。 **如何升级？** 用相同包名安装新版本，然后完全退出并重开 Harness。保留原 Profile 和账户目录即可延续使用。 **如何退出或卸载？** 先在设置页退出账户，再到 Plugins 卸载。[详细说明](docs/PRIVACY.md#断开与卸载)。 ## 了解更多 [思考强度](docs/REASONING.md) · [安装与排错](docs/INSTALLATION.md) · [兼容范围](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) · [数据与隐私](docs/PRIVACY.md) · [版本说明](RELEASE_NOTES.md) · [参与开发](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) 会话文本、所选图片和工具结果会发送至 OpenAI。登录凭证保存在本机未加密文件中，具有仅当前用户可读写的权限。本插件是独立社区项目，不隶属于 OpenAI 或 DeepSeek。 ### 插件头像 启用插件后，窗口右下角会显示「大肥鱼指挥 Codex」头像。图片随安装包提供，无需外部图片服务；头像不响应鼠标操作，不遮挡下方控件的点击。停用插件后自动移除。

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: DSH guard against self-repetition in streamed model output: detects a degeneration loop in reasoning or visible text, aborts the runaway turn and wakes the agent with a corrective notice.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-output-loop-guard

An **output self-repetition watchdog** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/).
When a model starts cycling the same short block instead of producing a tool call, the guard
aborts that generation and wakes the agent with a corrective notice — no human stop button,
and no human typing "continue".

- Bundle for DSH `>= 0.2.0-rc.2`, ESM, zero runtime dependencies.
- 21 self-contained regression checks (`npm test`).
- Calibrated against 27 real sessions / 1,783 assistant steps: **24 detections, 0 false positives**.

## The gap it fills

DSH ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-repeat-tool-reminder`, which only sees **duplicate tool calls**
(same tool, same arguments, 3/5/8 times in a row). A degeneration loop in the *reasoning
channel* is invisible to it. In the session that motivated this plugin:

- the model repeated `好。→（执行）→好。→Write.→…` in its reasoning for **112,109 characters**,
  emitted in **50,196 stream chunks over 126 seconds of continuous decoding**, and produced
  **zero tool calls** — so `repeat-tool-reminder` could not fire;
- automatic compaction never ran either: its trigger is
  `floor(min(W × 0.8, W − O − B))` ≈ 678k tokens for a 1M window with a 256k output cap,
  while the session peaked around 508k tokens;
- the loop only ended when the human pressed stop, and the polluted text stayed in the
  transcript, which made further loops more likely (self-imitation).

`output-loop-guard` listens on the live `agent/assistant-stream` frames and looks at the text itself.

## How it works

A sliding window over streamed output (1,200 characters by default, inspected every 64 new
characters) feeds four signals:

| Signal | Rule | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `repeated-block` | **Shortest-period** block (≥2 newlines, ≥2 distinct non-whitespace chars) repeated ≥6 times | Multi-line cycles, e.g. the 106-character `好。→（执行）→Write.` cycle |
| `dominant-gram` | One n-gram covers ≥55% of the window with ≥24 occurrences and spans ≥2 lines | Loops whose tail is ragged but where repetition already dominates |
| `repeated-line` | Single-line runs: ≥40 in the reasoning channel, ≥60 in visible text (`singleLineTextMinRepeats`, `0` disables) | Reasoning spinning on one line, runaway line duplication in answers |
| `flat-tic` | Whitespace-free short gram covering ≥25% of the window with ≥48 occurrences, **reasoning only** | Line-less tics (`好。好。好。…`) |

Two design rules keep it precise:

- **Only the shortest period counts.** When one line repeats, 2× and 3× the line length are also
  "periods"; judging on an arbitrary period turned an ordinary bullet list into a "multi-line
  cycle" during calibration. The guard therefore looks only at the shortest period and requires
  that block itself to span ≥2 newlines.
- **Channel awareness.** Repeated lines in visible output are usually legitimate content
  (generated fixtures, config files, lists), so the visible-text single-line threshold is higher
  (60) than the reasoning one (40), and line-less tics are only judged in the reasoning channel.
  Indentation runs, `====` / `----` rule lines and blank-line runs never trip the guard.

On detection the guard:

1. calls `agent.cancel({ kind: 'hook', reason: 'output-loop-guard: …' })` — the in-flight
   generation is aborted and recorded as interrupted, so the degenerate text stops growing;
2. calls `agent.steer(<notice>)` — because the signal is already aborted, `steer` upgrades to a
   **fresh turn** and wakes the driver, so the agent immediately continues with an explicit
   correction (stop restating, emit the next action or finish);
3. after `maxTripsPerTurn` trips in one turn it stops auto-continuing and only `inject`s the
   notice, so a genuinely broken model cannot spin forever.

## Install

The package is a DSH **bundle**: the loader reads `dsh.bundle.patch` from `package.json`
(`dsh.plugin.json` is optional metadata used by some local plugin indexes — the official runtime
ignores it), and `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `output-loop-guard` row.

```sh
# A. from a git host, pinned to a commit (requires `git` on the PATH of the DSH process)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "github:ADistanceThereIs/dsh-output-loop-guard#<commit>"

# B. from the release tarball — no git required
#    download dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz from the Releases page, then:
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add ./dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz

# C. straight from the release asset URL (needs Node to trust your system CA store)
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add \
  https://github.com/ADistanceThereIs/dsh-output-loop-guard/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-output-loop-guard-0.1.0.tgz
```

All three append the package to `dsh.profile.bundles` and compose the bundle's patch layer.
**Restart DSH for the row to activate.**

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-output-loop-guard
```

## Configuration

Override the row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's whole `config`,
so restate every key you want to keep):

```yaml
- id: output-loop-guard
  name: dsh-output-loop-guard
  config:
    dryRun: false                 # true = detect and log only, never cancel
    autoContinue: true            # wake the agent with the corrective notice
    maxTripsPerTurn: 2            # auto-continue budget per turn
    windowChars: 1200
    checkEveryChars: 64
    minPeriodRepeats: 6           # repeats required for a multi-line cycle
    singleLineMinRepeats: 40      # reasoning-channel single-line threshold
    singleLineTextMinRepeats: 60  # visible-text single-line threshold (0 = off)
    useDominantGram: true
    dominantGramCoverage: 0.55
    dominantGramMinCount: 24
    useFlatTic: true
    ticMinCount: 48
    ticMinCoverage: 0.25
    verbose: false
```

Start with `dryRun: true` if you want to observe detections in your own sessions before letting
the guard abort anything.

## Evidence

### Corpus calibration

Replayed over 27 real sessions / 1,783 assistant steps (a corpus containing both healthy and
degenerate real output):

- 24 detections, **0 false positives**;
- every loop step of the motivating session was caught, plus a same-pattern loop in an unrelated
  session;
- detection latency: the 112,109-character runaway was caught after **2,944 characters (2.6 %)**;
  other loops were caught within 1,152–7,808 characters — hundreds of milliseconds instead of
  20–126 seconds of spinning.

### Runtime verification

End-to-end check in a live DSH runtime, on a task engineered to repeat two lines 300 times. The
session log of that run contains:

```json
{"type":"turn/end","data":{"turn":1,"reason":{"kind":"aborted","reason":{"kind":"hook","reason":"output-loop-guard: repeated output (repeated-block)"}}}}
{"type":"assistant/message","interrupted":true}          // cut off after 9 repetitions, not 300
{"type":"user/message","source":{"kind":"output-loop-guard","form":"notice"}}
```

The agent then delivered the same content as a **file** instead of continuing to repeat it, which
is exactly the intended outcome: the guard stops runaway output, it does not kill the task.

### Regression suite

`npm test` runs 21 self-contained checks (no corpus needed): the real degeneracy must be aborted
(24,180-character stream caught after 576 characters), healthy long documents must be untouched,
realistic written output (lists, code blocks, tables, rule lines, fixtures) must not trip,
runaway written lines must trip, `dryRun` must not cancel, a disabled plugin must attach nothing,
and a throwing agent handle must not break the stream.

## Limitations

- Visible-text single-line repetition needs ≥60 identical consecutive lines (that protects
  legitimate fixtures and lists); disable with `singleLineTextMinRepeats: 0`.
- Detection is structural (periodicity and density), not semantic: a modified near-repeat may
  escape `repeated-block`, though `dominant-gram` / `flat-tic` usually covers it.
- Trips are counted per agent and per attempt; subagents do not share counters.
- A trip discards the tool call that step had not emitted yet — one retry is the price for not
  spinning for minutes. Use `dryRun` to observe first.

#

plugins.description: Adds a Restart row to the desktop app's sidebar foot beside Settings that restarts the app and reloads the page onto the newly installed plugin bundle.
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-sidebar-restart One row in the sidebar foot, beside the settings gear: restarts the DSH desktop app in a single click, instead of quitting from the tray and relaunching by hand. ![The Restart row above Settings in the desktop app](docs/usage-desktop.png) ![The same row in the mobile drawer, label included](docs/usage-phone.png) [![三种形态](docs/placement-options.png)](docs/placement-options.png) ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-sidebar-restart # once it is on npm ``` or straight from the repository: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:DONGBIN007/dsh-sidebar-restart ``` Then restart the app once by hand so the plugin loads — which is the last time you have to do that, since this button is what you use from then on. **Desktop only.** On a plain `dsh web` profile the row renders disabled and says why; there is no desktop process to replace there. If you wanted the *Web server* restarted, that is a different plugin ([`dsh-restart-button`](https://github.com/hadesybil-hub/dsh-restart-button)). ## What it does, in one line Adds a **Restart** row to the desktop app's sidebar foot beside Settings. Clicking it asks the Host to restart; a detached helper kills the Electron main process and the Host by PID, waits until both are gone, starts the app again, and the tab reloads itself once the replacement answers with a new boot id — so a plugin you installed a moment ago is actually running afterwards. ## What it looks like | Desktop app (wide sidebar) | Mobile drawer | |---|---| | ![desktop](docs/usage-desktop.png) | ![mobile](docs/usage-phone.png) | Both follow the host's own rule rather than a breakpoint of mine: the label appears exactly where the host shows one for the gear, i.e. when the sidebar is wide. In the narrow 56px rail the row stays icon-only and keeps the gear's 36×36 target. ## The control is a copy of the gear row next door The seat is `sidebar.footer.action` — "optional actions beside Settings at the sidebar foot". The shipped sidebar renders it as `footerActions`, a flex row that `footArea` lays out **above** `settingsArea` (the gear row). So in the plain host footer this control sits directly above the gear. It is deliberately styled as the gear's twin, with every value read from the shipped `.wCInkW_trigger` (ui-settings-general) and the seat's own sibling `.dsh-mobile-control__trigger`, which agree: | Property | Value | Why | |---|---|---| | colour | `--dsw-alias-label-primary` | the gear uses the **primary** label colour; a secondary-coloured icon beside it is a visible mismatch | | height | `42px` | the footer row height both host controls use | | padding | `0 10px 0 8px`, `gap 8px` | the gear's own padding and icon/label gap | | radius | `--dsw-radius-md` | the gear's radius, not the small one | | label | `14px / 22px`, `font: inherit` | the gear label's typography | | row box | `calc(100% + 4px)`, `margin 4px -2px` | the gear's row is `.wCInkW_triggerRow{width:calc(100% + 4px);margin:4px -2px}` — it bleeds 2px past the column on each side, so its content begins at `parentLeft − 2 + 8 = +6`. Without the same bleed this row's icon **and** label sit 2px to the right of the gear's, and the two never line up. This button *is* its own row, so it carries both the bleed and the padding. | Verified on a **real phone screenshot** (1216×2640, so ≈3.5 device px per CSS px), measuring the dark ink of each row directly: | row, on the device | icon ink left | label ink left | icon ink | row centre | |---|---|---|---|---| | before the bleed: 重启 | `73` | `157` | 50 | `2356.5` | | before the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 48 | `2531.5` | | after the bleed: 重启 | `66` | `150` | 50 | — | | after the bleed: 设置 | `67` | `150` | 48 | — | So the old geometry sat **+6 device px (≈2 CSS px)** right of the gear — the 2px the CSS predicted — and the shipped geometry lands within **1 device px** on the icon and **exactly 0** on the label. The two row centres are 175 device px apart, which is `175 / 3.5 = 50.0` CSS px — precisely the designed `21 + 4 + 4 + 21`. [![真机对齐：橙色线为齿轮图标左缘](docs/row-alignment-device.png)](docs/row-alignment-device.png) The orange line is the gear's own icon left edge. Before, the ↻ icon and the 重启 label both sit to its right; after, they land on it. The equivalent check against the host's shipped CSS in a controlled 340px column gives the same result to the hundredth: | row | icon left | label left | |---|---|---| | the gear | `5.67` | `29.67` | | this button, before the bleed | `7.67` (**+2.00**) | `31.67` (**+2.00**) | | this button, after the bleed | `5.67` (**0.00**) | `29.67` (**0.00**) | [![受控 CSS 校验](docs/row-alignment.png)](docs/row-alignment.png) One residual is **not** a CSS mismatch and is deliberately left alone: on the device the ↻ ink is 50px against the gear's 48px. Both icons are the host's own primitives at the host's own `wide ? 16 : 18`, drawn on the same 16px box with the same 1.3 stroke — a near-full circle simply carries more ink than a compact gear. Making the two inks match would mean drawing the shipped artwork below the size the host asks for, which is the one thing this row must not do. **The label follows the host's own `wide` convention** — no invented breakpoint. The gear's `TriggerContent` renders `wide ? + label : `, and `dsh-mobile`, the seat's other occupant, does `wide ?

plugins.description: DSH plugin: auto-compact long sessions after user idle time, before the KV cache expires.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-idle-compact [![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that prepares a compaction of a long session while you are away, before the model provider's KV cache expires, and lets you apply it with one click when you come back.

## Why

Providers cache the prompt prefix of a conversation for a few minutes. While the cache is warm, re-reading a long history is cheap. Once it expires, your next message re-bills the whole history at the full, uncached input price.

If you walk away from a long session, this plugin produces the compaction summary while the cache is still warm, so that summarization request is cheap. Nothing changes in your session until you decide to apply it.

## How it works

1. When a session finishes a turn and waits for you, a timer starts.
2. Any new activity in that session cancels the timer, whether it's you replying or the agent starting work.
3. When the timer fires, the plugin prepares a compaction only if all of these hold:
   - the agent is still idle and its last turn finished normally (not an error or a stop);
   - no background job or subagent is running for the session;
   - the session's context, measured with DSH's token meter, has reached the threshold.
4. Preparing runs exactly the summarization request DSH's `/compact` would make, and keeps the result. Your session is not changed.
5. An **Apply compaction** bar appears just above the message input, showing how many history items it covers.
6. Clicking it runs DSH's own `/compact` command, exactly as if you had typed it, and answers its summarization request with the prepared result, so no new model call is made. The conversation shows the usual `/compact` card with its "Compacted N history items" reply.

The prepared summary is only valid for the conversation it summarized. If you send another message (or the history changes in any other way), it is discarded and the button disappears; the next idle period that qualifies prepares a fresh one. If the conversation somehow differs at the moment you click, `/compact` makes its own model call instead of using a stale summary.

When the plugin starts or is reloaded (a DSH restart, a plugin update), sessions that are already waiting are timed from the end of their last turn. A session idle for less than the idle delay is timed for only the remaining seconds. A session idle for longer is skipped entirely, because the provider's cache has most likely expired and preparing would cost full price. It qualifies again after its next turn.

Subagent sessions are skipped, because they never wait for a user reply. If the agent is busy when the timer fires, nothing is prepared and this is logged.

## Settings

Open **Plugins → Idle Compact** in the DSH Web UI:

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Context length threshold (tokens) | `256000` | Prepare a compaction only when the session context has reached this length. |
| Idle time (seconds) | `300` (5 min) | How long you must go without replying before a compaction is prepared. |

Both fields take whole numbers of at least 1. Changes apply without a restart. A changed idle time takes effect the next time a session starts waiting.

You can also set them in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: idle-compact
  config:
    contextThresholdTokens: 200000
    idleSeconds: 240
```

## Install

Requires the DSH Web UI. Tested on DSH 0.2.1-alpha.3 and 0.2.1-rc.2; earlier versions are untested. The plugin uses DSH's authenticated `/api` routes, its settings-form components, and the area above the message input (`conversation.input.dock`).

```sh
dsh plugin add github:Arrosam/dsh-idle-compact
```

Or, in the Web UI, open **Plugins → Add plugin** and enter `github:Arrosam/dsh-idle-compact` or a local checkout path.

## Token cost

Each prepared compaction makes one summarization call to your model. It's cheap because the cache is warm, but it is spent even if you never click Apply or never return to that session. If most of your idle sessions are ones you abandon, raise the threshold.

Prepared summaries are kept in memory only. Restarting DSH discards them.

## Page endpoints

The browser half talks to the Host over two routes on DSH's own `/api` channel. DSH checks the browser's login and origin before either route runs, so other programs and other websites can't use them.

- `GET /api/idle-compact/events?sessionId=<id>`: a server-sent event stream. The first message is the session's current state, and another follows each change. Each message is `{ "prepared": false }`, or `{ "prepared": true, "items": <history items>, "tokens": <approx. tokens>, "applying": <boolean> }`.
- `POST /api/idle-compact/apply` with JSON `{ "sessionId": "<id>" }` applies the prepared compaction. Responses:

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | `{ "ok": <boolean>, "result": <command result> }` | `/compact` ran; `ok` is whether it succeeded. Its outcome also shows in the chat. |
| 200 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "command-unavailable" }` | The `/compact` command isn't available. |
| 400 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "bad-body" }` | The body isn't a JSON object with a non-empty string `sessionId`. |
| 404 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "no-session" }` | No live session has that id. |
| 409 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "not-prepared" }` | Nothing is prepared, or it went stale. |
| 409 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "applying" }` | An apply is already running for that session. |
| 500 | `{ "ok": false, "code": "failed", "message": "…" }` | Applying failed unexpectedly. |

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

The tests load the plugin into a real DSH runtime from your local DSH install and fake only the model provider and the browser connection. Set `DSH_RUNTIME_DIRS` (colon-separated `node_modules/@deepseek-ai` directories) to choose which runtimes to test against.

## Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host half: settings schema, public exports, and wiring of the parts below. |
| `src/idle-scheduler.js` | One idle timer per agent; aborts its work when the agent resumes. |
| `src/prepare.js` | Eligibility checks, and producing the summary on a detached copy of the session. |
| `src/replay.js` | Records the summarization request while preparing; replays it once on apply. |
| `src/prepared-store.js` | What is prepared for each session, and notifying the page when it changes. |
| `src/http.js` | The page's endpoints on DSH's authenticated `/api` channel. |
| `src/constants.js`, `src/util.js` | Shared names, values, and small helpers. |
| `client.js` | Browser half: the settings form on the Plugins page and the Apply bar above the message input. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the `idle-compact` row. |
| `locale/*.json`, `icon.svg` | Display metadata for the plugin manager. |
| `test/` | Tests that run the plugin inside a real DSH runtime. |

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Unofficial responsive remote Web UI bundle for DeepSeek Harness with native Desktop isolation.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Community Web UI · Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control English | [中文](README.zh.md) GitHub Release tarballs ship prebuilt `lib/` files and do not run a consumer-side build lifecycle. Source checkouts use `pnpm run build`.

   

Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Instant QR Pairing · Cross-Device PC Access · Mobile Touch Gestures · Cloudflare Tunnels · Secure Device Session

> Seamless remote access for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and desktop client sharing the **exact same interface**: pair an iPhone, Android smartphone, tablet, or another computer from the QR code next to settings. Both ends run the authentic official Web GUI — phones receive an injected portrait touch layer while remote computers enjoy the complete desktop workbench. Access is guarded by expiring pairing tokens and revocable sessions. Built-in LAN binding and optional Cloudflare quick tunnels enable effortless external access with persistent hostnames. This is an **unofficial community plugin** derived from `dsh-web` v0.4.5. It is structured as a cordis bundle: the host half manages pairing tokens, device sessions, `/api/pair` routes, the gated `/remote` channel, and LAN binding; the browser half renders the remote access trigger, QR pairing modal, live device roster, settings card, and mobile portrait touch adaptation. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek. ## What it does - **Entry**: a phone icon beside the settings button in both the expanded sidebar and the narrow rail; its tooltip and accessible label say "Remote access". - **Panel**: "Remote access" title, a "Pair a device" card with the status area ("Waiting for a device" + status badge), a large QR code, the pairing link with its copy button, Stop / Refresh QR actions, and the authorized-device roster (a device name inferred from User-Agent, online/offline, last active time, per-device unpair). Credential-bearing device ids and raw User-Agent values are never rendered. Both the phone and the PC use the same time-limited link: until it expires or the QR is refreshed, that link can pair several devices, each with its own device session. - **Phone side**: scanning the QR binds the phone with a time-limited token and reloads into the **official Web GUI** — there is no second interface to drift from. On touch phones, the plugin injects a responsive adaptation layer over the running UI for portrait and constrained landscape layouts (see "The mobile adaptation layer" below). The accept chain is cookieless (`/pair-accept` → `/pair-app`): the plugin itself serves the official shell, so the phone needs no harness browser-auth cookie at all. A reopen service worker (https origins) then owns later navigations to `/` from history, bookmarks, or tab restore, so the phone reopens straight into the app instead of a 401 dead end (see Security model). - **PC side**: the same link opens the full desktop Web GUI on another computer over the gated `/remote` channel; unpaired PCs see a guided blocking page (with a manual pair-token input) and no workspace data behind it. - **Security**: one active token at a time (a refresh invalidates the old link; the link stays re-usable within its expiry window so a scan handed between browsers can complete pairing; it expires). 停止 revokes every paired device and the current token — the `/remote` channel cuts them off on their next request. Pairing is this plugin's access control for the `/remote` channel; direct `/api` on a LAN-exposed bind is governed by the harness fence + browser auth (see Security model). Loopback (127.0.0.1) keeps using `/api` directly, and so does a page an application on this machine delivered — the desktop shell's `dsh-app://app/` or a `file:` page — because a pairing link is reachable only over the network. A paired device is a **full-control credential** (see Security model). - **LAN bind toggle**: the settings card writes a managed block into the profile `cordis.patch.yml` that pins the webserver bind to `0.0.0.0` (on) or `127.0.0.1` (off) — no `--host` command-line dance; an explicit `--host`/`--port` flag still wins. It maintains the matching host firewall rule (Windows Defender via netsh; Linux firewalld/ufw/iptables; other platforms report the firewall as unmanaged) and shows the live bind, the reachable LAN URLs, and the firewall state. - **Live status**: the desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; an `/api` posture probe reports any host whose `/api` fence the SDK leaves open, and the auto-tunnel state appears on the panel while the tunnel is starting. - **Self-update lives next door**: the one-click family update is its own plugin (`dsh-update`, the same sidebar foot seat), so turning remote access off — or disabling this plugin — never removes the update trigger. - **Desktop foot row**: on the wide sidebar the footer-action occupants share the official Settings trigger's line instead of stacking above it, so no single control owns a full-width row; any other foot block (the usage glance card, another plugin's) keeps a full row above them, and the 56px rail keeps the shell's stacked foot. ## The mobile adaptation layer The official desktop layout already auto-collapses the sidebar below 1024px. On top of that, while the viewport is portrait + coarse pointer + narrower than 1100px the plugin injects: - a CSS sheet keyed on CSS-Modules **semantic suffixes** (`[class$="_composerSeat"]`) so the selectors survive official rebuilds that only change hashes: 44px touch targets on the collapsed rail, 16px inputs (prevents iOS focus zoom), safe-area padding for the composer, compact type for the message list and sidebar, a column layout for the settings modal, and a full-width PlanReview card; - a **draggable whale button** as the entry to the collapsed sidebar (position persisted; wired to the official `ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`), hidden while the sidebar is expanded; - **gestures**: left-swipe collapses the sidebar, right-swipe in the conversation opens it; long-pressing a session row opens the same action menu as the desktop ellipsis; tapping a session row or anywhere outside the sidebar collapses it again; - **input behavior for touch**: Enter only inserts a newline (send goes through the send button), programmatic composer focus is suppressed (no spurious keyboards), and official tooltip bubbles are hidden because taps leave them stuck; - **mobile plugin scope**: while the layer is active, the right-hand details column and the desktop-oriented tool surfaces (SSH terminal, skill explorer, task board, git graph, pet, usage) are hidden - keyed on the L2 semantic roots (`data-dsh-plugin`), so ownership stays with the declaring plugin and class churn cannot resurrect them. These are render suppressions; the client bundles still load. Activation also closes the details panel through the official `ctx.layout.closeDetails()`. - a **manual opt-out**: `sessionStorage.dsh-remote-force-desktop = 1` disables the whole layer; touch-phone portrait and constrained landscape layouts are adapted, while the native Desktop app and wide desktop-browser layout stay on the official presentation. The paired remote desktop also runs in **host mode**: on this harness line the "configuration plane is local" behavior is a client-side branch on `connection.isLoopback`, and the channel boot script installs the transport hook (`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost = true`) before any boot entry. Host mode is **server-granted**: the hook is installed only when the device-gated app landing (`/pair-app`) published the grant marker ahead of the boot patch, so a shell served to an unpaired browser — a fence-open deployment — never poses as the machine owner. plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-opencode-pin · 把 OpenCode Go 的上游路由钉住

一个 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Host 插件：**把所有模型调用钉在 OpenCode Go 套餐上**，并保证每个请求都带 **稳定的 `x-opencode-session`**，从而让 OpenCode 的「会话 → 上游提供商」绑定在整段对话里不漂移。

---

[![awesome · DSH plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)

**源码**：<https://github.com/wobushiyoushen0214/dsh-opencode-pin>

## 安装

```sh
# 官方 CLI（插件市场里的同一条命令）
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-opencode-pin

# DSH 内置插件管理器
plugin_manager { action: "install_bundle", target: "dsh-opencode-pin" }
```

装好后：**设置 → 内置插件 → 页签「OpenCode 上游钉选」**。也可以从插件市场的卡片一键安装（搜 "OpenCode 上游钉选" 或 `dsh-opencode-pin`）。

---

## 0. 当前状态（本机已实测）

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 安装 | bundle `dsh-opencode-pin`，行 `opencode-pin`：`enabled` 且 `fiberPhase: active` |
| Config schema | `cordis_inspect_query Config.listConfigs` → `status: "schema"`，`packageDir` 指向 profile 链接；说明 `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 的 peer 路由在重启后生效 |
| 路由钉（**已在跑**） | 会话日志只有两条 `request/header`：`initial muyuan/deepseek-v4.1-flash` → `resume opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`（effort `high`、maxTokens `384000`）；重启后 13 条 `assistant/message` 全部由 `opencode-go` 服务，且**没有** provider 反复横跳 |
| 单测 | `node --test test/*.test.mjs` → 23 passed |
| 观测路由 | `GET /opencode-pin/status` 曾 404：已定位为注册时机 bug 并修复（见下），**需再重启一次生效** |

### 两个踩过的坑（都已在代码里修掉）

1. **`agent/request` 必须 `prepend` 才能钉住路由。** `dsh-agent` 自己的"会话模型选择"监听器也答 `agent/request`，它在外层 `await next()` 后用会话选择覆盖结果。插件原来注册在最内层，改写被吞掉，日志里表现为每步都 `muyuan -> opencode-go` 却钉不住；而且"会话选择 ≠ 最近 header"会被当成用户换模型，反复注入 `[model changed: …]` 通知。现在：`{ global: true, prepend: true }` + 通过 `sessionController.selectForNextRequest()` 把钉住的路由写成本会话 `model/selection`。
2. **`ctx.on('webServer', …)` 在 Cordis v4 里永不触发。** 服务就绪只以 `internal/service` 事件广播（`cordis/lib/index.js:849`）。而 `webServer` 由 web 端 bundle 挂载，插件在 profile bundle 之后激活时它可能还不存在 → 路由永远注册不上。正确写法是 `ctx.inject(['webServer'], (scoped) => …)`。
   现场对比（临时探针插件，两个路由同插件内并列）：
   ```text
   /opencode-pin-probe/inject   200  {"ok":true,"via":"ctx.inject"}
   /opencode-pin-probe/event    404
   ```

> 插件 JS 代码改动**必须重启应用**才会加载新一代模块（ESM 模块缓存）；只有 `cordis.patch.yml` 的配置改动走 HMR。

---

## 1. 为什么需要它（实测结论，非推测）

用 `scripts/evidence.mjs` 打真实请求（每次 1 token），OpenCode Go 会在响应头里明说自己用了哪个上游：

```text
x-opencode-endpoint-id:        novita-deepseek | luminal-dsv4.1flash | orcarouter-dsv4.1flash | ...
x-opencode-upstream-model-id:  deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | ...
x-zen-model:                   deepseek-v4.1-flash
x-opencode-log-id:             98b1140f-5350-4bce-8c02-19e1afa1f438
```

三个关键事实：

1. **同一个模型 id 由多个上游端点服务**（`novita-deepseek`、`luminal-dsv4.1flash`、`orcarouter-dsv4.1flash` …），
   `x-opencode-upstream-model-id` 甚至分两种命名体系：`deepseek-ai/...`（官方权重那一路）与 `deepseek/...`（第三方托管）。这就是「降智」的来源——落到哪个上游不由你选。
2. **路由由 `x-opencode-session` 决定，而且一旦分配就黏在那个 key 上**：
   - 同一 key 连续请求 → 始终同一个端点；
   - 换新 key → 落到「当前默认」端点（会随时间/负载整体变化）；
   - 官方文档明确要求：*"Send a stable session ID in `x-opencode-session` for each conversation so we can optimize routing and prompt caching."*
3. **不带这个头，请求直接被拒**：

   ```text
   HTTP 400  Request is missing x-opencode-session and cannot be routed efficiently.
   ```

而 DSH 只有部分路径会带 session：agent 主循环 / 子代理 / 标题 / 压缩都带，但
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review` 这类直接调 `ctx.llm.stream()` 的路径不带（OpenCode 官方文档的 "Known problematic clients" 里点名 DSH：*"Session information arrives on some model paths, but is missing on others."*）。
DSH 也不会把响应头暴露给插件，所以「现在到底落在哪个上游」平时是看不见的。

## 2. 它怎么做

| 机制 | 扩展点 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| 路由钉选 | `agent/request` waterfall | 在请求被**记入会话日志之前**把 provider/model 换成配置的目标（默认 `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`）。主循环与每个子代理都覆盖，用量归属与可回放 header 保持正确。 |
| 会话兜底注入 | `llm/stream` waterfall | 任何到达 LLM seam 却没有 `sessionId` 的调用，补齐为「发起该调用的对话身份」；落在 OpenCode 路由上的调用可改为共享一个被探测挑出来的 key（`shared` / `hunt` 模式）。 |
| 会话选择对齐 | `sessionController.agents.selectForNextRequest()`（facade 上若将来提升也接受；都没有则退回纯 waterfall，并在状态里报 `selectionApi: false`） | 把钉住的路由写成本会话的 `model/selection`。`dsh-agent` 会把"会话选择 ≠ 最近请求 header"当成用户换了模型，反复注入 `[model changed: ...]` 通知——对齐后不会误报，UI 的模型标签也与实际一致。 |
| 上游观测与挑选 | 自带 1-token 探测 | 因为 Harness 不给插件响应头，插件自己发探测请求，读出 `x-opencode-endpoint-id`，在 `hunt` 模式下**挑一个落在偏好端点上的 key 并全程复用**——这就是字面意义上的「钉住上游提供商」。 |

`hunt` 模式的做法：先用候选 key 并行探测（默认 4 个，每个 1 token），若某个 key 的端点命中 `probe.prefer`（例如 `["luminal-*"]`），就把这个 key 固定下来给所有会话用；超过 `probe.recheckMs` 会重新验证一次，发现漂移就再挑一轮并告警。

### 钉住上游端点（本插件的主要用途）

实测结论（本机，跨 1 小时+、跨两次应用重启）：

| key | 现在落到 | `x-opencode-upstream-model-id` |
|---|---|---|
| `probe-A` / `pin-live-a` | `luminal-dsv4.1flash` | `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`（官方权重命名那一路） |
| `pin-6` / `evidence-old` | `novita-deepseek` | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` |
| `pin-1` | `orcarouter-dsv4.1flash` | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` |
| 任何**新** key | 当前默认（观察期内从 luminal → novita → orcarouter 变过） | 随默认 |

两条关键规律：

1. **绑定黏在 key 上，且长期稳定**；换新 key 只会拿到"当前默认"。
2. 所以想要**非默认**端点（如 luminal），必须**复用当初落在那里、且一直黏着的旧 key** —— 这正是本插件 `probe.pool` / 记忆 key 的用途。

配置（`cordis.patch.yml` 里按行 id `opencode-pin` 覆盖，`config` 整体替换）：

```yaml
- id: opencode-pin
  name: "dsh-opencode-pin"
  config:
    pin:
      route: false                 # 不钉 provider 路由，只钉上游端点
    session:
      mode: shared                 # 所有 opencode 请求共用一个 key ⇒ 同一个上游
      models: [deepseek-v4.1-flash]  # 只钉这个模型（留空=该路由所有模型）
      key: probe-A                 # ← 换这一行就换上游：
                                   #   probe-A / pin-live-a → luminal-dsv4.1flash
                                   #   pin-6 / evidence-old → novita-deepseek
                                   #   pin-1               → orcarouter-dsv4.1flash
                                   #   任意新 key          → 当前默认端点
    probe:
      prefer: ["luminal-*"]        # hunt 模式的偏好端点（通配 *）
      pool: [probe-A, pin-live-a, pin-6, evidence-old, pin-1]  # 优先复用的历史 key
```

### 哪个端点算「DeepSeek 官方」？

同一模型 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` 在三个端点上的线上指纹（实测）：

| 端点 (`x-opencode-endpoint-id`) | `x-opencode-upstream-model-id` | 响应 `id` 形态 | 判断 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `luminal-dsv4.1flash` | **`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`** | `chatcmpl-ad9b3b1c` | HuggingFace 官方组织 `deepseek-ai/` 的仓库命名 ⇒ **官方权重那一路** |
| `novita-deepseek` | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 32 位 hex | OpenRouter 风格 vendor slug ⇒ 第三方托管 |
| `orcarouter-dsv4.1flash` | `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 56 位 hex | 同上 |

另外：端点空间是按模型分配的 —— `deepseek-v4-pro` 只有 `orcarouter-dsv4pro`；`deepseek-v4-flash` 只有 `novita-deepseek`；唯一名字就叫 `deepseek` 的端点只服务 `deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`，`deepseek-v4.1-flash` **拿不到**它（4 个不同 key 抽样均未出现）。

所以：**在 opencode-go 体系内，「官方」的上限就是 `luminal-dsv4.1flash`**（本插件的 `key: probe-A` 正指向它）。想要**真正的 DeepSeek 官方 API 直连**（`api.deepseek.com`），应当改用 DSH 自带路由而不是 opencode-go：

| 路由 | 凭据 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-account` | DSH 账号授权（`x-dsh-auth-token`） | 登录即用；`inferenceOrigin` 默认 `https://api.deepseek.com`；失败以 `ACCOUNT_QUOTA` 呈现 |
| `deepseek-official` | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | 需在 设置→模型 里填官方 API Key |

两条路由的默认目录都是 `deepseek-flash`（文本+图片，1M 上下文）与 `deepseek-v4-pro`（纯文本，1M），且模型 id 原样透传，任意官方模型 id 都能直接请求。

想让它**自愈**（定期校验绑定、漂移就自动换回一个命中的 key）：把 `session.mode` 改成 `hunt`。hunt 会**先验证 `pool` 里的历史 key**（而不是只探新 key，因为新 key 拿不到非默认端点），命中即用，超过 `probe.recheckMs`（默认 30 分钟）重新校验，发现漂移会在日志里告警并重挑。

监控漂移：面板点「探测一轮」，或 `curl "localhost:19387/opencode-pin/probe?keys=probe-A"`，看 `endpoint` 是否还是你钉的那个。

> 注意：`session.mode: shared` 会让该模型的所有请求（含标题/压缩/子代理）共用这一个 key —— 这是"钉上游"的代价与目的。想让别的模型保持原样，用 `session.models` 限定范围。

## 3. 安装

在 DSH 里用插件管理器安装（不会手写 profile 文件，也不需要 pnpm）：

```text
plugin_manager { action: "install_bundle", target: "/Users/lizhiwei/localProj/dsh-opencode-pin" }
```

安装后确认：

- `plugin_manager { action: "list_plugins" }` 里能看到行 `opencode-pin`（`application: applied` 表示已热挂载）；
- `GET http://127.0.0.1:19387/opencode-pin/status` 返回 JSON；
- 日志里出现 `opencode-pin: route pin on (opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash), session mode "conversation", hunt off`。

> 修改插件代码后需要重启应用才会加载新的 JS（`restart-required`）；只改 `cordis.patch.yml` 的配置会走 HMR。

## 4. 配置

配置走标准 DSH 方式：在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里按行 id 覆盖。**注意 patch 里的 `config` 是整体替换，不是深合并**，要改哪层就把那层写全。

```yaml
- id: opencode-pin
  name: "dsh-opencode-pin"
  config:
    pin:
      route: true                     # 强制所有调用走下面这个路由
      provider: opencode-go

plugins.description: A configurable direct channel for the DeepSeek Harness LLM egress: a keep-alive undici Agent with adjustable connect/headers/body/keep-alive timeouts, IPv4-forcing, HTTP/2 off by default, automatic stand-down behind a proxy, and a read-only status route. A minimal patch, one file, zero dependencies.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-undici-timeout

[![awesome · DSH plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

DSH 插件：给 LLM 出口（`globalThis.fetch` → Node 内置 undici）换一条**可配置超时 + 可保活复用**的直连通道。

English: [README.en.md](README.en.md)　·　发布流程: [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md)　·　收录条目: [`contrib/awesome-dsh-plugin/`](contrib/awesome-dsh-plugin/)

## 为什么需要它

- Node 内置 `fetch` 背后的 undici，`connectTimeout` 固定 **10s**（DNS+TCP+TLS 全算在内），
  没有环境变量/参数可调；
- 本机（WSL）直连 `opencode.ai` 的新建握手实测出现过 **11.6s**，双栈探测也常整轮
  `AggregateError`（IPv6 无出口 + IPv4 抖动）；
- pi-ai 每次重试都 `new OpenAI(...)` → `Shims.getDefaultFetch()` **当场读全局 fetch**，
  所以每次尝试都是新 TCP+TLS，被 10s 砍掉 → `TIMEOUT/TRANSPORT` → 重试又重连。
  今天（2026-10-13）的日志：87 次 TIMEOUT + 8 次 TRANSPORT，autoswitch 开代理 10 次。

对比：OpenCode（Go 客户端）全程复用一条已建立的 HTTP/2 连接，握手只发生一次，
所以同样的网络下它不超时。本插件就是把这套「长超时 + 保活复用」搬给 DSH。

## 这东西的寿命：它是一个补丁，不是一块功能

它存在的理由只有两条，而且两条都在**上游**，不是 DSH 的既定设计：

1. Node 内置 `fetch` 的 `connectTimeout` 固定 **10s** 且没有开关（Node/undici 上游行为）；
2. undici 8 把 `allowH2` 的默认值翻成 `true`，而 Cloudflare 边缘对 h2 上的 SSE 长流会
   回 `NGHTTP2_ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM`（上游默认值 × 边缘策略）。

这两条一旦在 DSH 侧被解决 —— 比如 LLM 层允许指定 dispatcher / 连接超时，或者换掉内置
fetch —— 本插件就**没有存在价值了**，直接卸掉：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-undici-timeout   # 或者删掉 profile 里那条 insert
```

判断「可以卸了」的依据（任一条成立即可）：

- 状态路由 `stats` 长期没有 `TIMEOUT`，且直连握手不再接近 10s；
- DSH 的 LLM 层能自己配连接超时 / 强制复用连接（看 release notes，或
  `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 里出现了对应配置项）；
- 上游把内置 fetch 换成了自带 Agent 的实现。

在那之前它是**最小补丁**：单文件、零依赖、只接管白名单域名、随时可摘。
所以只从 GitHub 分发，不发 npm、不进插件市场。

## 原理

```
agent 回合
 └─ dsh-llm-retry（重试）→ dsh-llm-pi-ai → pi-ai → new OpenAI({ fetch: undefined })
      → openai/client.mjs: this.fetch = Shims.getDefaultFetch()   ← 每次尝试当场读全局
      → 【本插件包装过的 globalThis.fetch】
           ├─ 命中 hosts 白名单 且 无代理 env → undici.fetch(url, { dispatcher: 自建 Agent })
           └─ 其它（代理模式 / 非白名单 / Request 输入）→ 原样透传给原来的 fetch
```

- 用**解析到的那份 undici**（`argv[1]` → profile 扫描 → bare）自建 `Agent`：
  `connect.timeout`、`headersTimeout`、`bodyTimeout`、`keepAliveTimeout/MaxTimeout`、
  `pipelining`、可选 `family`。
- **不碰 `setGlobalDispatcher`**：那是 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy` 的地盘（代理联动靠它），
  抢了会把 net-proxy 弄坏。本插件只接管「本来要走直连」的那部分流量。
- 代理 env（`http_proxy/https_proxy/ALL_PROXY` 任一大写或小写）在场时**自动让路**，
  由 harness 的代理层处理——所以能和 `dsh-net-proxy` / `dsh-net-autoswitch` 共存。

## 配置项（`cordis.patch.yml` 里本插件的 `config:`）

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | 总开关。`false` 时不改 fetch，状态路由仍在。 |
| `hosts` | `["opencode.ai"]` | 命中这些域名（含子域）才接管；`"*"` = 全部直连流量。 |
| `connectTimeoutMs` | `30000` | **核心项**。DNS+TCP+TLS 的总预算（内置固定 10s）。范围 1000–600000。 |
| `headersTimeoutMs` | `300000` | 等响应头。 |
| `bodyTimeoutMs` | `0` | 相邻 body 块间隔；`0`=关闭，卡流交给 pi-ai 的 `streamIdleTimeoutMs` 看门狗。 |
| `keepAliveTimeoutMs` | `60000` | 空闲连接保留时长（复用 = 不重握手）。 |
| `keepAliveMaxTimeoutMs` | `600000` | 保活上限。 |
| `pipelining` | `1` | 每连接并发请求数。 |
| `family` | `0` | `0`=跟随系统；`4`/`6`=强制 IP 族（本机 IPv6 无出口时 `4` 很划算）。 |
| `allowH2` | `false` | **⚠️ 见下面「h2 的坑」**。undici 8 把 `allowH2` 的默认值翻成了 `true`，不显式关掉，本插件会顺手把 LLM 出口从 h1 换成 h2。 |
| `autoSelectFamilyAttemptTimeoutMs` | `0` | Node happy-eyeballs 的**地址轮换间隔**（默认 250ms）。注意：尝试是**并行保留**的，这个值不是单地址的放弃窗口——黑洞地址实测默认与调大都会等到 connect 超时才死，改大只会拖慢轮换，一般别动。保留它只为极端调优。 |
| `delegateOnProxyEnv` | `true` | 有代理 env 时让路。 |
| `undiciPath` | `""` | 留空自动解析；可显式指到某份 `undici/index.js`。 |
| `probeOnStart` | `true` | 启动时打一次探针（默认打 LLM 网关的 models 端点，不花 token）。 |
| `probeUrl` / `probeTimeoutMs` | `…/zen/go/v1/models` / `15000` | 探针目标与超时。 |
| `logSlowMs` | `0` | >0 时把达到该耗时的请求写日志。 |
| `logFailures` | `true` | 失败请求记日志（含 cause）。 |
| `routePath` | `/_dsh/undici-timeout` | 状态路由。 |
| `logFile` | `$DSH_HOME/logs/dsh-undici-timeout/host.log` | 日志落盘。 |

## 安装

**只从 GitHub 分发**（本插件是上游行为的补丁，不发 npm、不上市场）：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mqnu00/dsh-undici-timeout
```

装完**重启 DSH** 生效。也可以钉住某个版本：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:mqnu00/dsh-undici-timeout#v0.1.1
```

零 npm 依赖、无构建步骤，所以 pnpm 不会弹 `allowBuilds` 授权（本插件没有任何
`prepare` / `install` 脚本）。⚠️ 别和下面路线 B 的 `file://` 直插**同时用**：
包内 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 insert id 也是 `undici-timeout`，同 id 冲突。

改完代码想知道「别人 clone 下来到底装不装得上」，本地跑一遍试装验证 —— 把包装进一个
临时 DSH_HOME 里的干净 profile、真启动一次、再请求插件自己的状态路由：

```bash
./scripts/trial-install.sh          # 走 tarball（等价于 GitHub Release 资产）
./scripts/trial-install.sh --git    # 走本地裸仓库 git+file://（等价于 github: 源）
./scripts/trial-install.sh --spec=github:mqnu00/dsh-undici-timeout   # 直接验真实远端
# 🎉 试装验证通过 = 组合成功 + 启动就绪 + 状态路由应答
```

打 tag / 建 Release 的步骤见 [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md)。

### 路线 B：file:// 直插 profile 用户层（改代码时用这条）

`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` 末尾追加：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: undici-timeout
      name: file:///home/mqnu/program/dsh/dsh-undici-timeout/lib/index.js?v=5
      config:
        enabled: true
        hosts: [opencode.ai]
        connectTimeoutMs: 30000
        # 本机 IPv6 无出口：别让地址族探测把预算烧在 10 个死地址上
        family: 4
        # undici 8 的 allowH2 默认是 true，不关掉就会把出口换成 h2（见「h2 的坑」）
        allowH2: false
        bodyTimeoutMs: 0
        keepAliveTimeoutMs: 60000
```

`dsh-hmr` 会监听该文件，**原地写** 2 秒内自动重挂（tmp+rename 会换 inode，收不到事件）。
⚠️ insert 行按 **id 幂等**：只改 `name`（换 `?v=`）或改 `config` 不会立刻重挂——要么**摘掉再插回**，
要么重启 DSH（HMR 的实测行为，和 dsh-net-autoswitch 一致）。
2026-10-15 复验：只把 `?v=4` 改成 `?v=5` 并加配置，HMR 确实重挂了（实例 id、`installedAt`
都换新），但**跑的还是旧模块代码** —— 日志里没有新加的 `h2=off` 字段，状态路由里也读不到
`allowH2`。原因就是同 id 的 entry 按**旧 URL** 重新 import。**摘掉（等 HMR 跑一轮）→ 再插回**，
这次 `?v=5` 才真正被 import，`h2=off` 出现在日志里。改代码务必按这个顺序。

## h2 的坑（2026-10-15 定位，`allowH2` 就是为它加的）

症状：插件明明在跑（`matched` 一直涨），却仍然「很频繁地失败」，重试日志里
`code=TRANSPORT` 暴涨。

根因是一条**静默换协议**：

| | 用的 undici | ALPN 实测 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 内置 `fetch`（Node 22 自带） | 6.24.1 | `http/1.1` | h1 |
| 本插件（`argv` 解析到 harness 那份） | 8.11.2 | `h2` | **h2** |

undici 8 把 `allowH2` 的默认值从 `false` 翻成了 `true`
（`lib/core/connect.js`: `allowH2 = allowH2 != null ? allowH2 : true`，
`lib/dispatcher/client.js`: “enabled by default”）。我们用 undici 8 建 Agent，
于是 LLM 出口从 h1 变成了 h2 —— 这不是本插件想要的，却实实在在换了传输层。

代价：`opencode.ai` 前面是 Cloudflare，h2 上的 SSE 长流会被边缘掐：

```
请求失败 CONNECTION（2275ms）…/chat/completions :: ERR_HTTP2_STREAM_ERROR / Stream closed with error code NGHTTP2_ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM
```

- 2026-10-15 当天：插件记了 **85 次失败，其中 79 次是 nghttp2 流错误**（93%），
  全部落在 `/chat/completions`（长流），`/models`（短请求）一次都没有；
- 首次出现 `ERR_HTTP2` 是 **2026-10-14T07:00**，即代理被关掉、插件开始全量接管直连之后；
  重试日志里 `TRANSPORT` 从 ~10/天 → **201/天**（10-14），`TIMEOUT` 则从 238/天 → 4/天
  （**插件治超时的效果是真的**，只是换了个失败形态）。

修法：`allowH2: false`（已进 DEFAULTS）。关掉之后复用一点没少：

| 4 连发（读完 body） | 新建连接数 | 耗时 |
|---|---|---|
| `allowH2: false` | 1 | 924ms → 383 → 363 → 374ms |
| `allowH2: true` | 1 | 947ms → 340 → 350 → 349ms |

即 h1 + `keepAliveTimeout` 的复用与 h2 等价，「不重握手」的目标照旧达成，
而 Cloudflare 那套 h2 流控彻底不参与。

2026-10-15 03:31 热更后（`?v=5`，`family=4` + `allowH2:false`）现场复验：
**75 秒内 22 个请求（全是 `/chat/completions`）20 成功 0 失败，`ERR_HTTP2` 0 次** ——
同一台机器、同一分钟里，改之前是 85 次失败/天、其中 93% 是这个 h2 流错误。

## 直连失败的另一半：20 个地址里的 10 个是死的（2026-10-15 实测）

`opencode.ai` 的 DNS 一次回 **10 个 IPv4 + 10 个 IPv6**，本机 **IPv6 无出口**
（`curl -6` 秒失败）。地址族探测（happy eyeballs）会把预算烧在这 10 个死地址上：

| 同一分钟内的对照 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 裸 TCP 连 10 个 IPv4 | 全部成功，245–1332ms |
| `curl`（双栈）/ `curl -4` | 8/8、5/5 成功，connect 0.27–0.46s |
| **内置 fetch**（undici 6） | **2/6 成功**，4 次 `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`，~2511ms |
| **插件 Agent，family=0** | **6/6 成功**，中位 352ms |
| 插件 Agent，family=4 | 6/6 成功，中位 379ms |

所以「插件生效了吗」的答案是：**生效，而且比内置通道明显强**；
但 `connectTimeoutMs: 30000` 救不了这种形态 —— 整轮在 ~1.0s / ~2.5s 就死掉，
是地址族探测把整轮判死，不是 10s 的 connect 预算不够。`family: 4` 能把这半边也堵上。

WSL 里直连脆弱、本机代理（`127.0.0.1:10808`）实测 3/3 HTTP 200（~0.9s）——
代理开着时插件按设计让路，也就不会被 h2 那套流控碰到。

## 状态/排障

```bash
# 读状态（在机器上直接 curl；Host 白名单只放行回环/本机网卡）
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3080/_dsh/undici-timeout | python3 -m json.tool

# 手动补一枪探针
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/_dsh/undici-timeout \
  -H 'x-dsh-undici-timeout: 1' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action":"probeNow"}'
```

- `stats.matched/ok/failed/byError`：接管了多少请求、失败怎么归类；
- `stats.delegatedProxy`：因代理 env 让路了多少（联动在工作就正常）；
- `stats.lastRequests`：最近 10 条（host/path/ms/status/error）；
- `lastProbe`：最近一次探针（启动探针也会写日志）。
- 日志：`~/.dsh/logs/dsh-undici-timeout/host.log`。

冒烟（不经过 DSH，验证解析与网络）：

`

plugins.description: DSH 技能中心：查看、开关、新建、按链接安装、删除（进回收站可恢复）DSH 技能。
plugins.readme_text:
# @suifengshiqu/skill-center

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh.md)

**Skill Center** adds one page to the DSH Web client where you can see every skill DSH can load from your own directories, read one, switch it on or off, create one, install one from a link, and delete one into a trash you can restore from.

It is a third-party DSH plugin, not an official DeepSeek product. Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

![The Skill Center panel, open over the composer](docs/shots/list.png)

## Screenshots

| | |
| --- | --- |
| ![The skill list](docs/shots/list.png) | ![Creating a skill](docs/shots/create.png) |
| **The list** — every skill DSH can load, with its switch, its provenance and its problems. The row above it is where a link goes. | **Creating one** — name, description and body, written into whichever destination is selected. |
| ![The trash](docs/shots/trash.png) | ![The delete confirmation](docs/shots/confirm.png) |
| **The trash** — what was deleted, where it came from, and one button to put it back. | **Deleting** — the confirmation says plainly that the skill goes to the trash, because a reversible delete is a different promise from an erase. |

The screenshots are rendered from the shipped browser bundle over the Host's own
`Modal` stylesheet, so the layout, colours and scrollbar are the ones the application
produces; only the surrounding application window is left out. `scripts/dev/render-shots.mjs`
regenerates them, in either theme.

## Where it appears

Two entry points, both opening the same page over one shared store:

- **Settings → Skill Center** — the settings section, so it sits with the rest of the configuration.
- **A `Skills` button in the composer**, in the input row beside the permission chip. It opens the page in a modal, which is the quick path for switching a skill on or off mid-task.

The composer button lives in `conversation.input.left`. That is the only composer seat a plugin may extend: the permission chip (`conversation.input.permission`) and the model picker (`conversation.input.model`) are `single` seats their own plugins already hold, so nothing can be inserted between them. The button also cannot deep-link to its settings section — `openSection` is internal to the settings shell — so it opens the page directly instead.

Both entries follow the Host's theme:

![The same panel in the light theme](docs/shots/list-light.png)

## What it does

- **Lists** the skills under `$DSH_HOME/skills` (default `~/.dsh/skills`), any directory the profile adds through `customSkillDirs`, and the current project's `<project>/.dsh/skills`.
- **Shows details** for one skill: description, path, frontmatter block and instruction body.
- **Searches** by name or description, and can hide the switched-off skills.
- **Switches a skill on or off** without losing it: everything else about the file, including your own frontmatter keys, is left alone.
- **Creates a skill** from a name, a description and a body.
- **Installs a skill from a link** — a GitHub repository, a `/tree/` path inside one, a `.zip`, or a single `SKILL.md`.
- **Deletes a skill into a trash**, and restores it from there.
- **Writes new skills where you choose** — the destination control offers every directory the profile makes available, and the host accepts nothing else.
- **Reports problems** the host would silently skip, such as a missing `description` or a name that is not kebab-case.
- Follows the Host's light or dark theme.

### Where new skills are written

The destinations come from the Host, not from the panel: `GET /roots` answers with the
profile's configured `customSkillDirs` followed by the default `$DSH_HOME/skills`. The
browser offers exactly that list, and `POST /create` and `POST /install` refuse a
directory outside it — so "choose where to write" does not become "write anywhere". With
one destination the control is a sentence; with several, each is a button, because the
path is the point.

### Where deletion is allowed to reach

Removing something the user wrote is the one destructive thing here, so it is bounded:

- **Only DSH's own skills.** The trash covers the global roots (the DSH home and any `customSkillDirs`). A project root — `<project>/.dsh/skills`, which is under version control — is never touched: Skill Center may switch such a skill on or off, but it will not move it out of a repository.
- **Only skills DSH can actually load.** A skill with broken frontmatter may have been misread, which is a reason to leave it alone rather than to move it.
- **Never through a link.** A symbolic link, or a Windows junction (which `lstat` reports as an ordinary directory), is refused by comparing the resolved path with the requested one.
- **Never a plain erase.** The bundle is moved into `~/.dsh/skill-center/trash` with a record of where it came from, and the panel can put it back byte-for-byte. Emptying the trash is a separate, confirmed action.
- **Never a half-move.** Everything is validated before anything moves, and a move that cannot be recorded is rolled back. Because `rename` cannot cross volumes, a failed move falls back to copy-then-remove — copy first, so a failure leaves the original in place.

### What installing a link will and will not do

The download is treated as hostile input: entry paths may not escape the target, a bundle must have a `SKILL.md` with a name DSH accepts and a description DSH requires, an existing name is refused rather than overwritten, and nothing is written until every one of those checks has passed. Private archives and Zip64 are refused. Links to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `.local`) are not fetched, and a single download is capped at 8 MB and 800 entries.

### Which layouts are discovered

Matching the Host's own filesystem provider exactly, a skill is a directory bundle `<name>/SKILL.md` or a flat `<name>.md`, **at the top level of a skills root**. Nested `**/SKILL.md` is deliberately not discovered.

This matters when installing from a GitHub download: a repository ZIP extracts to one folder, and copying *that* folder into `~/.dsh/skills` leaves every bundle one level too deep, where neither DSH nor this panel will find it. Move the bundle folders themselves into the skills root.

## What it does not do

- No other agents' directories (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …).
- No Git repositories, no skill marketplace, no automatic updates.
- No creating or importing skills.
- No Trash.
- Nothing outside the two roots above is ever read or written.

## How switching a skill off works

Skill Center writes the two flags the DSH filesystem provider already understands into the skill's own frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: What it is for.
disable-model-invocation: true
user-invocable: false
---
```

Switching the skill back on removes exactly those two keys, restoring the document byte-for-byte. Because the flags live in the file:

- the state survives restarts and is visible to any other tool;
- the skill disappears from the model catalogue and the `/` menu, but stays on disk;
- an interrupted write cannot leave a half-written document — the file is replaced atomically.

A skill whose frontmatter cannot be parsed is listed with a diagnosis and its switch is disabled, so Skill Center never rewrites a document it does not understand.

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web client (tested against `0.2.0-rc.2`).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.

## Install

From npm, which needs nothing on the machine but DSH:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add @suifengshiqu/skill-center
```

From source, if you want to change it:

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/a766513648-lgtm/dsh-skill-center.git
cd dsh-skill-center
npm install
npm run verify                   # type check, build, tests
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add .
```

Or from a tarball you built yourself:

```powershell
npm pack
dsh plugin --profile <your-profile> add .\suifengshiqu-skill-center-0.1.0.tgz
```

Then **restart DSH** — the host half is loaded once at start-up, so a page refresh
alone is not enough — and open **Settings → Skill Center**.

> Installing this package by its git URL doe

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-superpowers-verified

**A fork of [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) for the
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH)** —
the full Superpowers methodology (brainstorming, planning, TDD, systematic
debugging, subagent-driven execution) adapted to run on DSH, installed
**verifiably and reversibly**.

Superpowers is an agentic software-development methodology by
[Jesse Vincent](https://blog.fsck.com) / [Prime Radiant](https://primeradiant.com);
this fork adapts it to DeepSeek Harness. It is not affiliated with or endorsed
by the Superpowers project, Prime Radiant, or DeepSeek.

[![tests](https://github.com/dkeviv/dsh-superpowers-verified/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dkeviv/dsh-superpowers-verified/actions/workflows/tests.yml)

```
15 skills · DeepSeek Harness (DSH) · 86 tests · live-catalog verification · non-destructive install
```

**Keywords:** Superpowers fork for DeepSeek Harness · DSH skills ·
obra/superpowers port · DeepSeek coding agent skills · TDD · subagent-driven
development · agentic workflow for DSH · `superpowers-dsh` alternative ·
DeepSeek Harness 技能包 · 超级技能

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/dkeviv/dsh-superpowers-verified.git
cd dsh-superpowers-verified
./bin/install.sh --dry-run     # see exactly what will change
./bin/install.sh
```

Then start a fresh DSH session and send `Let's make a react todo list`. A
working install invokes **brainstorming** and asks what you actually want
before writing any code.

**Uninstall reverses it exactly:**

```bash
./bin/install.sh --uninstall
```

## Why this fork exists

Superpowers' skills are mostly harness-neutral, but two things don't carry over
to DSH, and this fork supplies them:

**1. DSH has no session-start hook.** Upstream injects `using-superpowers` via a
`SessionStart` hook (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Muse, Pi, …). DSH's
`dsh-hooks-*` packages *provide* hooks to other harnesses rather than consuming
them. DSH's equivalent channel is its user-global instruction file,
`$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`, loaded every turn of every session — so the bootstrap
goes there, inside self-managed markers.

**2. DSH has a different tool vocabulary.** Nothing here is named `Agent`,
`Task`, `TodoWrite`, or `Skill`. DSH provides `skill`, `todo_write`,
`subagent`/`subagent_fork`/`workflow`, native plan mode, and a file sandbox.
[`references/dsh-tools.md`](references/dsh-tools.md) is the translation layer.
Upstream's platform-adaptation list is rewritten to name DSH **only**: the
Claude Code reference file left in place describes nested-subagent depth tuning
and a `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` variable that do not exist here.

**3. DSH skill names carry no namespace.** Upstream cross-references its own
skills as `superpowers:writing-plans`, but DSH rejects a colon in a skill name
outright, so those references are unresolvable as written. See
[Known limitations](#known-limitations) — this is the one upstream
incompatibility this fork documents rather than silently patches.

## What makes this fork different

There are several Superpowers ports for DSH. This one is built around two
properties rather than around features:

**Verification against the real catalog, not against prose.** `bin/verify.sh`
mounts DSH's own skill registry and filesystem provider and asks what actually
resolves — then checks it. Around that, `tests/run.sh` is 86 checks covering
snapshot integrity, fidelity against the vendored copy, idempotency, hostile
`AGENTS.md` inputs, migration paths, and uninstall, plus a GitHub Actions matrix
on Ubuntu and macOS. Most ports *assert* DSH compatibility; this one
demonstrates it, and fails loudly when it does not hold.

**An install that cannot damage your setup.** The suite runs entirely in a
throwaway prefix, so it never touches your real skill root or `AGENTS.md`. The
installer owns only the region between its markers, preserves your own
`AGENTS.md` content, appends rather than reorders, and uninstalls exactly what
it installed. Updating means `git pull && ./bin/install.sh` — idempotent, so
running it twice is safe.

**A pinned, auditable snapshot.** The skills are a vendored copy of upstream at
an exact commit ([`vendor/superpowers/README.md`](vendor/superpowers/README.md)),
so installs are offline, reproducible, and diffable against upstream. All
DSH-specific code lives outside `vendor/`.

| | This fork | Typical DSH port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Install mechanism | Filesystem installer into DSH's native skill roots | Cordis plugin bundle via `dsh plugin add` |
| Compatibility evidence | 86-check suite + live-catalog verifier + 2-OS CI | Prose assertion |
| Install reversibility | Marked-block ownership, exact uninstall | Varies |
| Upstream skills | Pinned commit, vendored | Usually synced at build time |

The plugin-bundle approach is more idiomatic to DSH's internals; the
filesystem approach needs no plugin layer and keeps every change reviewable in
your own config. Pick whichever fits how you run DSH.

## What you get

All 15 Superpowers skills:

| Skill | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `using-superpowers` | Entry point: how to find and use skills |
| `brainstorming` | Draw out intent before building |
| `writing-plans` | Break approved designs into bite-sized tasks |
| `executing-plans` | Inline plan execution, one review at the end |
| `subagent-driven-development` | Fresh subagent per task, reviewed |
| `dispatching-parallel-agents` | Fan independent work out in parallel |
| `systematic-debugging` | Root-cause discipline before fixes |
| `test-driven-development` | RED-GREEN-REFACTOR enforcement |
| `verification-before-completion` | Evidence before claims |
| `requesting-code-review` | Pre-merge review |
| `receiving-code-review` | Evaluate feedback on technical merit |
| `finishing-a-development-branch` | Integrate completed work safely |
| `using-git-worktrees` | Isolated workspaces |
| `writing-skills` | Author and test new skills |
| `diagnosing-superpowers` | Post-mortem a session from its transcript |

## Options

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--target <dir>` | Skill root (default `$DSH_AGENTS_HOME/skills` or `~/.agents/skills`) |
| `--dsh-home <dir>` | DSH home holding `AGENTS.md` (default `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`) |
| `--no-skills` / `--no-bootstrap` | Do just one half |
| `--dry-run` | Print intended changes, write nothing |
| `--uninstall` | Reverse the install |

## Verification

Two independent things, both re-runnable:

```bash
tests/run.sh          # 86 checks, offline, no writes outside a temp dir
bin/verify.sh         # audit a LIVE install against DSH's own skill catalog
```

`bin/verify.sh` is the interesting one. It does not read your files and guess —
it mounts DSH's real skill registry and filesystem provider in a bare Cordis
context (the same code the running harness uses), asks for the resolved
catalog, and checks the answers:

```bash
$ ./bin/verify.sh
Verifying Superpowers for DSH
  modules: /Users/you/.npm/_npx/…/node_modules
  skills:  /Users/you/.agents/skills
  AGENTS:  /Users/you/.dsh/AGENTS.md

  ✓ catalog resolves completely        22 skills
  ✓ every vendored skill resolves from --target   15/15 at …/.agents/skills
  ✓ no resolved skill name uses a namespace
  ✓ every installed skill has a loadable name
  ✓ no skill is shadowed by $DSH_HOME/skills
  ✓ DSH reference file installed
  ✓ adaptation list names DSH
  ✓ no other harness is advertised
  ✓ namespace workaround is documented
  ✓ bootstrap present in AGENTS.md     one balanced block
  ! upstream namespace references      46 references use superpowers:<name>; agents must strip the prefix

10 passed, 1 warnings, 0 failed
```

It exits non-zero when something is actually wrong, so it works in CI or a
pre-commit hook. It catches, among others: a skill that is installed but does
not resolve (including one silently skipped by DSH for an illegal name), a
skill shadowed by a higher-precedence root, a platform list that were reverted
to upstream, an unpaired bootstrap marker, and a missing reference file.
